pages.brief: A group of roadside giants: a huge tire in Michigan, an oversized chest of drawers in North Carolina, a giant violin in Nova Scotia, a big artichoke in California, a ketchup bottle in Illinois, a cuckoo clock in Ohio, an ear of corn in Minnesota, and a rubber stamp in Ohio.

pages.text: A Map to Amazement UNITED STATES MEXICO Stop and Look Roadside attractions grab people’s attention and cause them to stop. Do you want to know what The Thing is in Arizona? You’ll just have to pull off the road to find out!
pages.brief: A map shows the United States and Mexico, with a route leading to a roadside attraction in Arizona. A traveler pulls off the road and stops to look, ready to discover what The Thing really is.

books.title: Coral Reefs
books.art_why: Real coral reefs, marine animals, and people can be photographed.

pages.text: Underwater Communities Coral reefs are huge ocean communities. Millions of animals and sea plants live in them. Coral reefs are very busy places. Many kinds of coral make up reefs. Corals aren’t rocks or plants. They are tiny animals called polyps (PAH-lips). Most polyps are smaller than a pea.
pages.brief: A busy underwater coral reef filled with many kinds of coral, sea plants, and sea animals. Tiny polyp animals, most smaller than a pea, live in the reef. The reef is a huge, busy ocean community.

pages.text: Kinds of Coral There are two kinds of coral. The first kind is hard corals. These corals have hard skeletons. Over time, thousands of polyp skeletons help build a reef. Algae (AL-jee) live in the bodies of these corals. Algae are simple cousins of plants. The algae are food for the corals.
pages.brief: Hard corals underwater, showing their hard skeletons. Thousands of tiny polyp skeletons build the reef over time. Algae live inside the bodies of these corals, and the algae serve as food for the corals.

pages.text: Soft corals are the second kind of coral. They often look like trees or other plants. These corals can bend with the water currents. Algae live in the bodies of some of them. Many corals are named for what they look like. Brain corals look like brains. Sea fans look like open fans. Sea pens look like old-fashioned pens made from big feathers.
pages.brief: Soft corals underwater, bending with the water currents and looking like trees or other plants. Some have algae living inside their bodies. Brain corals look like brains, sea fans look like open fans, and sea pens look like old-fashioned feather pens.

pages.text: A Busy Home Thousands of fish of all sizes, shapes, and colors live on reefs. They depend on the reef for food and safety. Shrimp, lobsters, crabs, and sea stars feed on reefs. The holes in reefs are good places for animals to hide.
pages.brief: A busy reef home with thousands of fish of many sizes, shapes, and colors swimming around coral. Shrimp, lobsters, crabs, and sea stars feed on the reef. Holes and spaces in the reef give animals places to hide and stay safe.

pages.text: Where Corals Live Most coral reefs are close to shore in warm parts of the world. Corals need certain things to stay healthy. They need algae for food. They must be near the water’s surface so the algae can get enough sunlight. Also, both corals and algae need water that is not too warm or cold. There are three kinds of coral reefs. Fringing reefs are close to the shore.
pages.brief: Coral reefs in warm parts of the world close to shore. Corals sit near the water’s surface so algae inside them can get sunlight. Algae provide food, and the water is not too warm or cold. A fringing reef lies close to the shoreline.

pages.text: Barrier reefs have a Wowser! large, deep area of water between the reef and the shore.
pages.brief: An underwater view of a barrier reef with a large, deep area of water between the reef and the shore. Coral grows along the barrier reef while the wide, deep gap separates it from land.

pages.text: Atolls, the third type of reef, are shaped like circles. They form around the edges of a slowly sinking island. After the island sinks, a small body of water called a lagoon forms in the center.
pages.brief: A circular atoll reef formed around the edges of a slowly sinking island. After the island sinks, a small body of water called a lagoon sits in the center. Coral rings the atoll around the lagoon and surrounding ocean.

pages.text: Dangers to Coral Reefs Coral reefs are very fragile. Many things can harm them. People are the biggest cause of harm. People burn huge amounts of coal, oil, and gas to power cars and factories and to heat and cool buildings. Burning coal, oil, and gas is making Earth’s air and water warmer. Warmer ocean water causes many problems for coral reefs.
pages.brief: A fragile coral reef underwater, with people on land using cars and factories and heating and cooling buildings by burning coal, oil, and gas. The burning makes Earth’s air and water warmer, and warmer ocean water brings problems to the reef.

pages.text: Corals are getting sick. Coral diseases can destroy a big reef in just weeks. Warmer water is also causing corals to lose their algae. Without algae, corals have no food. They also lose their color and turn white. Three-fourths of all coral reefs have this problem.
pages.brief: Corals on a reef look sick and turn white after losing their algae. Without algae the corals have no food. Coral disease spreads across the reef, and many corals show damage. The white, unhealthy corals cover a large part of the reef.

pages.text: Other things harm coral reefs, too. Some people use poisons and explosives when they fish. Boats can break off large pieces of reefs. Dirt and trash can smother them. Boats can also leak gas and oil. Gas and oil hurt coral, plants, and fish.
pages.brief: People fish near a coral reef using harmful poisons and explosives, while a boat leaks gas and oil. Trash and dirt smother the corals, and boats break off large pieces of reef. The gas, oil, and damage harm coral, plants, and fish.

pages.text: Protecting Coral Reefs Coral reefs are beautiful. They are also important for many reasons. Reefs help protect coasts from storms and floods. They provide food for many kinds of fish that people eat. Some reef plants and animals are used for medicines. Many countries try to protect their reefs. They have written laws and rules to keep reefs safe. But people do not always follow those laws and rules.
pages.brief: A healthy coral reef near a coastline with storm waves breaking offshore, helping protect the coast from storms and floods. Fish swim around reef plants and animals used for food and medicine, while people work to protect the reef.

pages.text: Half of the world’s reefs have been destroyed. Most of the others are in trouble. Scientists are working to help coral reefs. Each of us can help, too, even if we don’t live near an ocean. Never throw things in the water. Learn about what people do that makes ocean water too warm. We can all help protect coral reefs. Then all the living things on coral reefs will continue to have homes and food. Coral Nurseries.
pages.brief: Scientist divers tend a coral nursery underwater, caring for young corals as they work to help reefs. Nearby, reef animals have homes and food. On shore, people learn about warming ocean water and keep trash out of the water to help protect coral reefs.

books.title: Wiggly Worms
books.art_why: Earthworms are real animals that can be photographed.

pages.text: Small Animals, Big Changes What do you know about earthworms? These small animals change the soil in big ways.
pages.brief: A close-up view of several earthworms moving through dark, moist soil. Around them, bits of soil are loosened and shifted, showing the small animals in the place where they live and work. The worms are the focus of the scene.

pages.text: Earthworm Bodies An earthworm’s body is shaped like one tube wrapped around the outside of another tube. On the outside is a tube of muscle, and on the inside is a tube that breaks down food.
pages.brief: A realistic close-up view of an earthworm's body, shown as two tubes, one around the other. The outer tube is muscle, and the inner tube is where food is broken down. The worm rests in moist soil.

pages.text: The body of an earthworm is made up of many parts. Each part is shaped like a ring, and it can bend and stretch. Earthworm Facts.
pages.brief: A close-up of an earthworm's body, with many ring-shaped parts visible along its length. The body is bent and stretched, and each ring-shaped part is clearly shown in this realistic view. The close view focuses on the many parts that make up the worm.

pages.text: Earthworms move by stretching out their bodies and pulling themselves forward. Short, tough hairs on earthworms’ bellies help them hold onto the ground.
pages.brief: Earthworms move across the ground by stretching their bodies out and pulling themselves forward. A close view shows the short, tough hairs on their bellies touching the ground and helping them hold on as they move.

pages.text: Slimy Worms! Earthworms’ bodies are covered in slime. The slime helps keep earthworms cool and wet. It also helps earthworms slide through soil.
pages.brief: A close-up of an earthworm covered in shiny slime. The slime keeps the worm cool and wet as it slides through dark soil. The worm's body looks moist and smooth in the damp surroundings. A realistic view.

pages.text: After worms mate, a small ball of slime forms. The slime dries into a cocoon where baby worms can grow. Later, baby worms come out of the cocoon. How do earthworms breathe?
pages.brief: A small ball of slime near an earthworm in the soil. The slime dries into a cocoon, and later a baby worm comes out of the cocoon. The scene shows the cocoon and the young worm in the place where they develop.

pages.text: Earthworm Behavior Earthworms build long tunnels underground. The tunnels protect worms from heat and sunlight and they also help earthworms hide from hungry animals.
pages.brief: Earthworms build long tunnels underground. The realistic view shows worms inside the tunnels, protected from heat and sunlight and hidden from hungry animals. Dark soil surrounds the long, winding spaces the worms have made. A close view.

pages.text: Earthworms are sometimes called night crawlers because they come out at night to feed. They use their mouths to pull dead leaves and plants into their tunnels.
pages.brief: Earthworms come out at night to feed. In the dark, a worm uses its mouth to pull dead leaves and plants into its tunnel. The scene shows the night crawler at the tunnel opening with dead leaves and plant bits nearby.

pages.text: Earthworms Are Good for the Soil Farmers love earthworms! When earthworms dig tunnels, they create space in the soil. The space helps plants get the water and air they require to grow.
pages.brief: Farmers love earthworms. In a farm field, earthworms dig tunnels that create space in the soil. The spaces help plants get the water and air they need to grow. The view shows worms in the soil beneath plants.

pages.text: Some people raise earthworms on worm farms. The earthworms eat food scraps, turning them into rich soil. Earthworm waste helps plants grow big and healthy.
pages.brief: On a worm farm, earthworms eat food scraps, turning them into rich soil. A realistic close view shows the worms among food scraps and dark, rich soil. The soil helps plants grow big and healthy.

pages.text: Wanted: Earthworms! Farmers aren’t the only ones who love earthworms. Moles, rats, and toads love juicy night crawlers. They love to eat them! Worms make good fishing bait because fish think earthworms are tasty, too. Earthworms are important food for these and other animals.
pages.brief: Moles, rats, and toads are shown near juicy night crawlers in the soil, ready to eat them. A fish is also shown near an earthworm, since fish think earthworms are tasty. Earthworms are important food for these and other animals.

pages.text: Earthworms may be small, but they have a big job. Earthworms help plants grow! In one night, an earthworm can...
pages.brief: Earthworms may be small, but they have a big job helping plants grow. A realistic close view shows earthworms in soil near growing plants. The scene focuses on the worm's small body and the big work it does in one night.

books.title: Taj Mahal
books.art_why: The book covers Mughal rulers and the 1600s building of the Taj Mahal, before photographs could show these events.

pages.text: The Taj Mahal Hundreds of years ago, the Mughal (MOO-guhl) family ruled parts of India. They were rich and powerful rulers. They built many beautiful buildings that still stand today. Of all the places the Mughal people built, the most famous is the Taj Mahal (TAJ muh-HAHL) in Agra, India.
pages.brief: The Taj Mahal in Agra, India, stands as the most famous of the beautiful buildings made by the rich and powerful Mughal rulers, who ruled parts of India hundreds of years ago. Its grand form shows the wealth and power of the Mughal family.

pages.text: The Taj Mahal is a memorial with beautiful buildings, walls, and gates. It also has peaceful gardens and lovely pools of water. Shah Jahan (SHAH jah-HAHN) was an important Mughal ruler. He built the Taj Mahal over three hundred years ago for his wife after she died. Her name was Mumtaz Mahal (moom- TAHZ muh-HAHL). Shah Jahan wanted to make a beautiful burial place for her. He wanted people to remember her for a long time.
pages.brief: Shah Jahan, an important Mughal ruler, is shown with the Taj Mahal memorial he built for his wife, Mumtaz Mahal, after she died. The memorial includes beautiful buildings, walls, gates, peaceful gardens, and lovely pools of water.

pages.text: The Great Gate People enter the Taj Mahal through the Great Gate. Visitors can see the main building through the door of the gate. The huge white building is where Shah Jahan and Mumtaz Mahal are buried. Four tall, thin towers are around it.
pages.brief: Visitors enter the Taj Mahal through the Great Gate and see the huge white main building through the gate's doorway. Four tall, thin towers stand around the white building where Shah Jahan and Mumtaz Mahal are buried.

pages.text: The Main Building Some of the Taj Mahal’s buildings are made of red sandstone. The main building and the towers around it are made of white stone called marble. The Taj Mahal buildings have many beautiful things, both inside and outside. Artists used thousands of colorful stones to make flowers, butterflies, and other pictures on the walls. Different kinds of shiny gems were used as well.
pages.brief: The main building and its surrounding towers are shown in white marble, while some other Taj Mahal buildings are made of red sandstone. Artists decorate the walls with thousands of colorful stones forming flowers, butterflies, and other pictures, along with different kinds of shiny gems.

pages.text: Visitors can go inside the main building, where Shah Jahan and his wife are buried. A coffin for Mumtaz Mahal is in the center of the room. Her husband’s coffin is beside hers. Both coffins are empty. They are only for people to view. The real burial places are in a room under the main floor.
pages.brief: Visitors inside the main building see the coffin of Mumtaz Mahal in the center of the room and the coffin of Shah Jahan beside hers. Both coffins are empty and are only for people to view; the real burial places are in a room under the main floor.

pages.text: A Love Story Shah Jahan met his wife-to-be when he was fifteen and she was fourteen. They were married five years later. He gave her the title Mumtaz Mahal, which means “Chosen One of the Palace.” She was his wife and also his close friend.
pages.brief: A young Shah Jahan meets his wife-to-be when he is fifteen and she is fourteen. Five years later they marry, and he names her Mumtaz Mahal, his chosen one of the palace, as his wife and close friend.

pages.text: When Mumtaz died, Shah Jahan was heartbroken. People said he was so sad that his beard turned white, and he cried so much, he needed glasses.
pages.brief: A heartbroken Shah Jahan is shown after Mumtaz Mahal died. People said his sadness was so great that his beard turned white, and he cried so much that he needed glasses. His grief is clear.

pages.text: The Buildings Go Up After Mumtaz Mahal died, Shah Jahan returned to his capital city of Agra, India. He decided to build the Taj Mahal in Agra beside the Yamuna (YAH-moo-nah) River. Shah Jahan began building the Taj Mahal in 1632, about a year after Mumtaz Mahal died.
pages.brief: After Mumtaz Mahal died, Shah Jahan returns to his capital city of Agra, India. He decides to build the Taj Mahal beside the Yamuna River, and building begins in 1632, about a year after her death.

pages.text: It was a big job. Twenty thousand workers helped build the Taj Mahal. One thousand elephants helped carry things. Builders and painters came from all over the world. Huge pieces of white marble were pulled on carts by oxen. Workers used ropes to move the marble into place. The work was finished in 1653.
pages.brief: Twenty thousand workers and one thousand elephants help build the Taj Mahal. Builders and painters come from all over the world, oxen pull carts carrying huge pieces of white marble, and workers use ropes to move the marble into place before the work is finished in 1653.

pages.text: The Taj Mahal Today After Shah Jahan died, the Taj Mahal was forgotten. People stole many of the gems and stones from its walls. They also took gold lamps, beautiful rugs, and other things. Since then, people have fixed some of the damage at the Taj Mahal. Today, air pollution is the biggest danger. Pollution from factories damages the buildings and ruins the white marble. People work to keep the Taj Mahal safe. They moved some factories farther away. Groups of people work to fix harm caused by air pollution.
pages.brief: After Shah Jahan died, the Taj Mahal was forgotten, and people stole gems, stones, gold lamps, rugs, and other things from it. Today air pollution from factories is the biggest danger, damaging the buildings and ruining the white marble, while people work to keep it safe and fix the harm.

pages.text: A Lasting Memorial Shah Jahan wanted to make a place for people to enjoy forever. Today, the Taj Mahal is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. Many people visit every day to view the beautiful buildings and gardens. Hundreds of years have passed since the Taj Mahal was built. It is still one of the most beautiful places in the world.
pages.brief: Many people visit the Taj Mahal every day to view its beautiful buildings and gardens. Today it is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World, and hundreds of years after it was built, it is still one of the most beautiful places in the world.

books.title: Real-Life Multiplication
books.art_why: Real-world objects like buttons, dimes, toys, and pizzas are best shown in photographs.

pages.text: You and your friends are making an art project for a school art show. You are in charge of bringing buttons for the project. You empty the button box onto the table. There are so many buttons! Could there be twenty buttons? Fifty? How can you figure it out? Sometimes you need to find out how many objects are in a large group. Counting them is one way. But counting this many objects is tricky! When you count, you have to be sure that • you keep track of the buttons you have counted already • you don’t count any of the buttons twice • you don’t miss any buttons Real Life Multiplication.
pages.brief: A child and friends sit at a table working on an art project for a school art show. The child has emptied a box of many buttons onto the table. The buttons are spread out, ready to be counted.

pages.text: One way to make objects easier to count is to group them. Once the objects are in groups, you can add the number in each group to find the total. There are four dimes in one hand. There are six dimes in the other hand. You can add the number of dimes in each group to find the total. There are ten dimes in all. Real Life Multiplication.
pages.brief: Two open hands are shown holding dimes. One hand holds four dimes, and the other hand holds six dimes. The dimes in each hand are grouped separately, and the two groups can be added to find the total.

pages.text: There are three groups of baseball bats in the picture. There are two groups of four bats. There is one group of one bat. You can add the number of bats in each group to find the total. There are nine bats in all.
pages.brief: Three groups of baseball bats are arranged for counting. Two groups each contain four bats, and one group contains a single bat. The bats in each group can be added to find the total number of bats.

pages.text: There is one ring on each finger of one hand. There are five rings in the first group. There is one ring on each finger of the other hand. There are five rings in the second group. There are two rings in the group on the table. You can add the number of rings in each group to find the total. There are twelve rings in all. Real Life Multiplication.
pages.brief: Two hands are shown with a ring on each finger, five rings per hand. A separate group of two rings rests on the table. The rings are grouped so the numbers can be added to find the total.

pages.text: There are two groups with ten cubes in each group. In the third group, there is one cube. You can add the number of cubes in each group to find the total. There are twenty-one cubes in all.
pages.brief: Three groups of cubes are shown. Two groups each contain ten cubes, and the third group contains one cube. The cubes are arranged in separate groups so their numbers can be added to find the total.

pages.text: There are three groups with two feet in each group. You can add the number of feet to find the total. There are six feet in all. Real Life Multiplication.
pages.brief: Three groups of feet are shown in the picture. Each group contains exactly two feet. The feet are separated into groups so the numbers can be added together to find the total number of feet.

pages.text: There is another way to find a total. You can skip-count if there is the same number of objects in each group. There are three groups of two feet. There is the same number in each group. So, you can skip-count to find the total. There are six feet in all.
pages.brief: Three groups of feet are shown in the picture, with two feet in each group. All three groups are the same size, so the feet can be skip-counted to find the total number of feet.

pages.text: Each butterfly has two antennae. There are six butterflies. You can add the number of antennae to find the total. There are twelve antennae in all. Real Life Multiplication.
pages.brief: Six butterflies are shown in the picture, each with two antennae. The antennae are visible on the butterflies. The numbers of antennae can be added across the butterflies to find the total number of antennae.

pages.text: There are six groups of two antennae. There is the same number in each group. So, you can also skip-count to find the total. There are twelve antennae in all.
pages.brief: Six groups of two antennae are shown in the picture. Each group has the same number of antennae. Because the groups are equal, the antennae can be skip-counted to find the total number of antennae.

pages.text: There are three groups of toy cars. There are three cars in each group. You can add to find the total. There are nine toy cars in all. Real Life Multiplication.
pages.brief: Three groups of toy cars are shown in the picture. Each group contains three toy cars. The cars are arranged in separate groups so their numbers can be added to find the total number of toy cars.
